sent-Sea turtles hatch from eggs buried in beach sand. The babies often come out of their nests at night. On a naturally dark beach, they crawl toward the brighter, open horizon over the ocean and away from darker dunes. Bright lights from buildings can lead them in the wrong direction. Some beach towns turn off or shield lights during nesting season. Only a few hatchlings survive to adulthood, so protecting their route to the sea matters.

sent-Frogs start their lives as tiny eggs in the water. The eggs hatch into tadpoles that have tails and swim like fish. Slowly, the tadpoles grow legs and lose their tails. Then they hop onto land as frogs. This change is called a life cycle.
